Every programming language in the ML fam.why: Stated at the level of the family: ML was designed around a static type system, and Wikipedia says ML-derived languages are best known for their static type systems. Rated unlikely rather than very_unlikely because it can also be generalised from members (Standard ML, OCaml, F#).

F# is statically typed..why: F#'s typing is given by name in its article and in texts on the language; the by-name route of the F# queries.

sources.note: Infobox typing discipline: static, strong, inferred.

notes: TBox rule edit. No real exceptions known: Standard ML, Caml, OCaml, F#, Alice ML and the other ML dialects are statically typed with type inference. F# is the well-known member (not OCaml, whose name ends in 'ml' and hints at the family). Dynamic typing is a plausible counterfactual for a functional family (Lisp is dynamic) and clearly false. The near query asks Java, whose answer (static) differs from the new answer; Python was avoided because its answer (dynamic) equals the new one.
